name: Console
what it is: The console block: 3.7 m wide on the centreline against the forward bulkhead, with a way to the forward corner windows each side of it. From aft: a stainless grab rail along its edge; a desk that slopes up 11° with two rows of flush panels on a dark field, and the three control heads in its after edge, at the hand; a level strip with the propulsion and thruster panels, each in line ahead of its levers; an upstand leaning back 20° with the displays set into it under glass, lower in the middle so that the sea is seen over it ahead of the wheel (nothing ahead of the wheel over 1.225 m, nothing else over 1.315 m: calculation JS4-402 asked 1.22 and 1.33). Below the desk a cabinet of five bays, each with two doors on hinges, a quarter-turn lock and louvres: they open to a tap, and the units that are not seen stand behind them on shelves.

name: Master's chair
what it is: A high-backed pilot chair in black leather at the conning position, to port of the wheel: headrest, armrests, a footrest, on a pedestal that runs on a track let into the deck and turns. A tap on its pedestal runs it aft or forward; a tap on its seat turns it.

name: Watch officer's chair
what it is: The second pilot chair, at the radar: like the master's, on its own track.

name: Chart table
what it is: The chart table against the aft wall, with three drawers for folded charts, which run out to a tap, and the chart in use on its top. She navigates on paper charts; the chart system on the console is an aid.

name: Bookshelf, nautical publications
what it is: Tide tables, the list of lights, the radio signals list, the signal code and the ship's own manuals, behind a fiddle rail.

name: Binoculars box
what it is: Two 7 × 50 binoculars in a varnished box on the console block's port end. Its lid lifts to a tap.

name: Stair well and rail
what it is: The head of the crew stair from the saloon, railed on its inboard side, with a self-closing gate across the top where one comes up: it opens forward, away from the well.

name: Watchkeeper's table
what it is: A table in the starboard forward corner, beside the pantry: a top of light varnished wood with her profile engraved in it and a cup well in its corner, a drawer that runs out to a tap, the deck log under its own lamp. (It takes the place of the fold-down log desk that hung under the port window.)

name: Settee
what it is: A settee in black leather along the port side under the windows, forward of the wing door, for the pilot and for whoever waits on the bridge.

name: Handrail under the sills, port
what it is: Stainless tube on brackets under the sills, from the console block to the port side and aft along it over the settee: something to hold in a seaway while looking out.

name: Handrail under the sills, starboard
what it is: Stainless tube on brackets under the sills, from the console block to the starboard side and aft along it over the watchkeeper's table.

name: Hook rail
what it is: A board of light wood with four brass hooks under the after port window, for oilskins and the watch's lifejackets.

name: Door, corridor to wheelhouse
what it is: The door from the crew corridor. It opens into the wheelhouse and is kept shut at night to keep the corridor's light off the glass.

name: Deck covering
what it is: Blue sheet vinyl on the steel deck, turned up every wall as a coved skirting; ribbed rubber mats at the helm and before the console; the two tracks the pilot chairs run on are let into it.

name: Deckhead lining
what it is: Strips of off-white panel running athwartships under the compass deck, a shadow gap between each two; the cable trays lie above them.

name: Overhead grab rail, port
what it is: A rail under the deckhead to hold on to in a seaway.

name: Overhead grab rail, starboard
what it is: A rail under the deckhead to hold on to in a seaway.

name: Overhead console
what it is: Two sloped consoles under the deckhead over the block, either side of the instruments that hang between them: the camera monitor to port, the two VHF sets to starboard. They hang above the windows' head, so that they hide nothing the glass would show.

name: Sun blinds
what it is: A roller blind of tinted film in a cassette at the head of each forward window, on two guide wires. A tap draws one down, and lets it up again.

name: Door to the port wing
what it is: A weathertight door, hinged on its forward edge, with a glazed upper half and a 0.15 m sill. It stands opposite the starboard one: the Minato Maru's stood in the aft corner, where the boards and their locker now have the wall to themselves.

name: Door to the starboard wing
what it is: A weathertight door, hinged on its forward edge, with a glazed upper half and a 0.15 m sill.

name: Wheelhouse plating, linings and windows
what it is: The house itself: plated outside, lined inside, five forward windows raked 10° under a visor, and windows down both sides: glass over 224° of the horizon from the helm.

name: Wing bulwarks, port
what it is: A plated bulwark 1.1 m high round the wing, with a varnished cap rail.

name: Wing bulwarks, starboard
what it is: A plated bulwark 1.1 m high round the wing, with a varnished cap rail.

name: Radar display
what it is: The radar picture, with target tracking: the display and its keyboard at the watch officer's chair, set in the console's upstand under a hood against the daylight.

name: Radar processor
what it is: The radar's processor unit: it takes the scanner's signal, the heading and the position, and gives the picture to the display and to the chart system.

name: Radar scanner
what it is: An X-band scanner on the mast platform: a turning unit and a 1.8 m array, 14.2 m above the waterline.

name: AIS transponder
what it is: Sends her name, position, course and speed on VHF and shows the ships that send theirs.

name: Electronic chart system
what it is: Her position on an electronic chart, with the radar's and the AIS's targets laid over it. An aid: the paper chart on the chart table is the chart she is navigated on.

name: GPS navigator
what it is: Position, course and speed over the ground from the satellites; it gives them to every set that needs them, the radios among them.

name: Echo sounder
what it is: The depth under the keel, drawn as a trace, with a shallow-water alarm.

name: Speed log
what it is: The speed through the water from a sensor in the bottom; shown on the conning display.

name: Navigation data distributor
what it is: Takes each sensor's sentences once and gives a buffered copy to every listener, so that no set can pull another's line down.

name: Conning display
what it is: Heading, rudder angle, both engines' revolutions, speed, depth and wind on one screen in front of the master's chair.

name: Satellite compass processor
what it is: Works out her true heading and rate of turn from the two antennas in the dome on the compass deck. It is the heading every set steers and plots by.

name: Autopilot control unit
what it is: Sets and holds a heading; it steers through the steering control unit like the wheel does.

name: Wind display
what it is: Wind direction and speed relative to the ship: a round instrument hung under the deckhead ahead of the helm.

name: Heading repeater, overhead
what it is: Her true heading on a compass card, hung under the deckhead ahead of the helm where the whole bridge reads it.

name: Bridge clock
what it is: A quartz clock on ship's time, hung under the deckhead. Its own battery.

name: Navigation network switch
what it is: The Ethernet switch of the navigation network.

name: Compass periscope
what it is: The magnetic compass on the compass deck, read from the helm through a tube and a mirror: it stands directly under the binnacle.

name: Bearing repeater, port wing
what it is: A heading repeater under an azimuth ring on a pelorus stand, to take bearings from the wing.

name: Bearing repeater, starboard wing
what it is: A heading repeater under an azimuth ring on a pelorus stand, to take bearings from the wing.

name: Ship's clock
what it is: A brass bulkhead clock over the chart table.

name: Barometer
what it is: An aneroid barometer.

name: Clinometer
what it is: Shows her list in degrees.

name: AIS antenna
what it is: The AIS's own VHF whip, 1.4 m.

name: GPS antenna
what it is: The GPS navigator's antenna dome.

name: Satellite compass antenna
what it is: Two satellite antennas in one dome, a known distance apart along her length: the heading is the direction from one to the other.

name: Magnetic compass and binnacle
what it is: The standard compass, on the centreline clear of steel and wiring, with a dimmed lamp. It needs no power to point.

name: AIS position antenna
what it is: A small satellite antenna for the AIS's own position fix.

name: Wind sensor
what it is: A cup anemometer and a vane at the starboard end of the flag yard.

name: Steering stand and wheel
what it is: The helm: an eight-spoke wheel on a stand. The wheel's shaft runs through a flanged bearing into the helm unit on the stand's top, where it turns two transmitters, one for each control system, and the pointer on the unit's lid that shows the rudder ordered. Where the wheel is put, the rudders follow: four degrees of wheel for one of rudder, and the spoke with the brass cap upright when they are amidships. On the page the wheel turns with the rudder.

name: Steering control system No. 1
where, if hidden: inside the steering stand, port half
what it is: The first of two control systems that have nothing in common. It compares the rudder ordered (by the wheel's first transmitter, or the autopilot) with the angle fed back from the gear and works the valves of power unit No. 1. Its supply comes from that power unit's own circuit in the steering-gear room, and its cables go down the port side.

name: Steering control system No. 2
where, if hidden: inside the steering stand, starboard half
what it is: The second control system: the wheel's second transmitter, its own amplifier, the valves of power unit No. 2, a supply from that unit's circuit (which comes by the emergency switchboard), and cables down the starboard side. Either system steers her alone; the selector on the stand chooses.

name: Steering mode selector and tiller
what it is: Chooses the control system (No. 1 or No. 2) and hand steering, autopilot or the tiller. The tiller works the valves of the chosen power unit directly (non-follow-up): the rudders move while it is held over, and it needs neither amplifier. It stands in a gate, a slot across the ship; a tap holds it over or lets it go.

name: Heading repeater
what it is: The heading in figures, low on the stand's face: read by looking down, not through it.

name: Rudder angle indicator, overhead
what it is: The rudders' true angle, from the transmitter on the steering gear: a round instrument hung under the deckhead, read from anywhere in the wheelhouse.

name: Rudder angle indicator, console
what it is: A second indicator among the propulsion instruments. It sits on the console, not on a stand-off, so that the sea is seen over it (calculation JS4-402).

name: Engine control lever, port
what it is: One lever for the port engine: ahead or astern through the gearbox, then revolutions. It stands in the desk's after edge, at the hand, and its panel and the engine instruments are read over it. A control head: the lever turns on a shaft inside the housing and comes up through a slot in its top plate; a drum on the shaft closes the slot under it, and where the arm crosses the plate is its reading on the scale beside it, from full astern through stop to full ahead. Pushed forward is ahead. A tap moves it a notch, and the port engine's lever on each wing moves with it.

name: Engine control lever, starboard
what it is: One lever for the starboard engine, a control head like the port one's. A tap moves it a notch, and its fellow on each wing moves with it.

name: Bow thruster lever
what it is: Thrust to port or starboard from the tunnel thruster in the bow. A control head whose slot lies across the ship: the lever is pushed the way her bow is to go. A tap moves it a notch, with its fellow on each wing.

name: Propulsion control panel
what it is: Which station has control (bridge, a wing, or the engine control room), engine start and stop, and an emergency stop for each engine under a flap. On the level strip, in line ahead of the two engine levers and under their instruments.

name: Bow thruster panel
what it is: Start, stop, running lamp and the motor's current. On the level strip, in line ahead of the thruster lever.

name: Engine instrument panel
what it is: Revolutions of both engines, their oil pressure and cooling-water temperature. Low on the console, straight ahead of the wheel: the sea is seen over it (calculation JS4-402).

name: Propulsion control unit, bridge
what it is: Reads the levers at the three stations, decides which one commands, and sends the orders to the engine room over two CAN lines.

name: Wing control station, port
what it is: Engine and thruster levers at the hand, and over them, in an upright face that leans back to the eye, a rudder angle indicator and a revolution indicator, each in line ahead of the lever it answers and read over it; at the outboard forward corner of the wing, for berthing port side to. The levers are outboard: standing at them she is seen along her side, and across the bow past the house to 45° on the other side.

name: Wing control station, starboard
what it is: Engine and thruster levers at the hand, and over them, in an upright face, a rudder angle indicator and a revolution indicator read over the levers; at the outboard forward corner of the wing, for berthing starboard side to. The levers are outboard, as on the port wing.

name: VHF radiotelephone No. 1, with DSC
what it is: The distress and calling set: 25 W, digital selective calling on channel 70 with her position from the GPS. In the starboard overhead console, with its handset in a cradle beside it on a coiled cord: the handset lifts to a tap.

name: VHF radiotelephone No. 2
what it is: The second set, for port and working channels, and the spare for the first: in the starboard overhead console.

name: NAVTEX receiver
what it is: Prints navigational and weather warnings broadcast on 518 kHz: on a bracket on the after wall over the chart table, where the warnings are plotted.

name: Portable VHF sets and charger
what it is: Three waterproof two-way sets for the survival craft, kept charged in their rack.

name: Radar transponder, port
what it is: A search and rescue transponder beside the port door, to be taken into a survival craft: it answers a searching radar. Its own battery.

name: Radar transponder, starboard
what it is: The second transponder, beside the starboard door. Its own battery.

name: Float-free EPIRB
what it is: A satellite distress beacon in a bracket that lets it go and float free if she sinks. Its own battery.

name: VHF antenna No. 1
what it is: A 3 m whip on the starboard side.

name: VHF antenna No. 2
what it is: A 3 m whip on the port side.

name: NAVTEX antenna
what it is: A short active antenna for 518 kHz.

name: Public address and general alarm amplifier
what it is: A 240 W amplifier with the general alarm's tone generator: seven short blasts and a long one on every loudspeaker aboard.

name: Public address and talkback panel
what it is: The microphone, the zone keys (car deck, saloon, crew, open decks), the general alarm key, and the talkback keys for the two wings, the mooring stations, the ramp and the engine control room.

name: Telephone
what it is: The ship's automatic telephone: cabins, mess, galley, engine control room. Its handset lies in a cradle beside it on a coiled cord, and lifts to a tap.

name: Sound-powered telephone
what it is: Speaks to the engine control room and the steering-gear room with no supply at all: the voice makes the current, and a hand crank rings the other end. A cased wall set on the console block's starboard end; its handset lifts to a tap.

name: General alarm push button
what it is: Sounds the general alarm from the door.

name: Loudspeaker, wheelhouse
what it is: A loudspeaker in the deckhead.

name: Talkback station, port wing
what it is: A weatherproof loudspeaking station on the house side.

name: Talkback station, starboard wing
what it is: A weatherproof loudspeaking station on the house side.

name: Loudhailer
what it is: A horn loudspeaker on the mast platform, for hailing and for the fog signal's listening watch.

name: Machinery alarm panel
what it is: The engine room's alarms in groups, with a buzzer: the bridge sees that something is wrong below, and whether the engineer has accepted it.

name: Bridge watch alarm
what it is: Asks the watch to press a button every few minutes at night. Unanswered, it calls the master's cabin, then the general alarm.

name: Watch alarm reset, chart table
what it is: A reset button at the chart table.

name: Camera monitor
what it is: Four cameras on one screen: the bow ramp, the car deck, the stern and the engine room.

name: Ramp, hatch and watertight door panel
what it is: A lamp for the bow ramp, each hatch and each of the five watertight doors: green when shut and secured, red when not.

name: Camera recorder
what it is: Records the cameras.

name: Fire detection panel
what it is: The addressable fire detection panel: it names the detector that has answered, sounds the bells, and after two minutes unaccepted, the general alarm. It has a standby battery of its own.

name: Manual call point
what it is: Break the glass to give the alarm.

name: Smoke detector
what it is: An optical smoke detector on loop 1.

name: Sprinkler head, port
what it is: A pendent sprinkler head in the deckhead: its glass bulb bursts at 68 °C and lets the water out. The sprinkler main it stands on is not registered yet.

name: Sprinkler head, starboard
what it is: A pendent sprinkler head in the deckhead. The sprinkler main it stands on is not registered yet.

name: Fire extinguisher, CO₂ 5 kg
what it is: For the electrical equipment: carbon dioxide leaves nothing behind.

name: Fire extinguisher, powder 6 kg
what it is: Dry powder, beside the port door.

name: Fire hose box
what it is: A 15 m hose with a dual-purpose nozzle, coiled in its box beside the hydrant.

name: Navigation light panel
what it is: A switch, a fuse and a lamp-failure indicator for each lantern, on a mimic of the ship; a change-over switch between its two supplies. On the console block's apron, under the desk.

name: Sidelight, port
what it is: Red, from right ahead to 22.5° abaft the port beam: on the bulwark's rail at the wing's outer end, with a screen board inboard of it.

name: Sidelight, starboard
what it is: Green, from right ahead to 22.5° abaft the starboard beam: on the bulwark's rail, with a screen board inboard of it.

name: Masthead light
what it is: White, over 225° ahead, on the front of the mast above the radar, its lens clear over the posts of the radar platform.

name: Anchor light
what it is: White, all round, on the crown of the mast.

name: Stern light
what it is: White, over 135° astern: on the centreline at the stern, on the bulwark's rail over the stern door, with a screen forward of it so that it is not seen from forward of the beam.

name: Not-under-command lights, upper pair
what it is: Red, all round: two heights of them in a vertical line, 2 m apart, say she cannot keep out of the way. Each height is a pair of lanterns, one either side of the mast, lit together: a single lantern beside the mast would be hidden by it over 35° of the horizon, and no more than 6° is allowed.

name: Not-under-command lights, lower pair
what it is: Red, all round: the lower pair, 2 m under the upper.

name: Whistle
what it is: Two air horns on the front of the mast, sounded by compressed air.

name: Whistle panel
what it is: A push button for the whistle and a timer for the fog signal (one long blast every two minutes when under way).

name: Searchlight control
what it is: A joystick that turns and tilts the searchlight, and its lamp switch.

name: Wiper and window wash panel
what it is: Each wiper on, off or intermittent, and the wash. A tap on a switch turns it a step, and its wiper runs.

name: Window wiper, starboard
what it is: A pendulum wiper on the outside of the glass, hung from its spindle in the window's head under the visor; its motor is inside, over the blind. A tap starts and stops it.

name: Window wiper, centre
what it is: A pendulum wiper on the outside of the glass ahead of the wheel, hung from its spindle in the window's head under the visor; its motor is inside, over the blind. A tap starts and stops it.

name: Window wiper, port
what it is: A pendulum wiper on the outside of the glass, hung from its spindle in the window's head under the visor; its motor is inside, over the blind. A tap starts and stops it.

name: Clear-view screen, port
what it is: A glass disc spinning in a ring in the window ahead of the master's chair: spray and rain are thrown off it, and it is clear where the window is tinted. Its motor is at its middle, carried by a tube from the rail under the window. A tap starts and stops it.

name: Clear-view screen, starboard
what it is: The second clear-view screen, in the window ahead of the watch officer's chair.

name: Window heating junction box
what it is: Where the forward windows' heated glass is fed and switched: a box let into the lining below the sill, with its lamp.

name: Searchlight
what it is: A 1 kW searchlight on the compass deck, turned from the console.

name: Flag locker
what it is: The signal flags of the international code, each rolled in its own pigeonhole.

name: Daylight signalling lamp
what it is: A hand lamp for Morse by day, on its hook beside the starboard door with its socket.

name: Deckhead light
what it is: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

name: Deckhead light
what it is: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

name: Deckhead light
what it is: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

name: Deckhead light
what it is: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

name: Deckhead light
what it is: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

name: Deckhead light
what it is: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

name: Deckhead light
what it is: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

name: Deckhead light
what it is: A round downlight in the deckhead, for work in harbour and by day.

name: Chart lamp
what it is: A dimmed lamp on a stalk, red or white, that lights the chart and nothing else.

name: Night light, red, port
what it is: A red light over the console: enough to find a switch by, without spoiling the night vision.

name: Night light, red, starboard
what it is: A red light over the console.

name: Emergency light
what it is: Lights by itself when the main supply fails.

name: Transitional light
what it is: A 24 V lamp on the general service battery: it lights at once when the supply fails, before the emergency generator has started.

name: Wing light, port
what it is: A bulkhead light on the house side.

name: Wing light, starboard
what it is: A bulkhead light on the house side.

name: Dimmer panel
what it is: Dims the instruments, the red night lights over the console and the chart lamp. A tap on a knob turns it a step: the night lights and the chart lamp go out and come on with it, and the displays darken when the instruments are turned down.

name: Foredeck floodlight, port
what it is: Lights the car deck forward and the ramp.

name: Foredeck floodlight, starboard
what it is: Lights the car deck forward and the ramp.

name: Wheelhouse distribution board BD1
what it is: 230 V, from the lighting board in the engine control room: eight ways for the bridge's general services.

name: Emergency distribution board BD2
what it is: 230 V, from the emergency switchboard: six ways for what must not go dark.

name: 24 V DC panel DC1, navigation and control
what it is: 24 V from the general service battery: fifteen fused ways, a voltmeter and an earth-fault lamp.

name: 24 V DC panel DC2, radio
what it is: 24 V from the radio battery: five fused ways, a voltmeter and the charger-failure alarm.

name: Sockets below the sill, port
what it is: A double 230 V socket in the lining below the forward sill, port side.

name: Console socket
what it is: A 230 V socket on the console block's apron.

name: Console heaters
where, if hidden: inside the console, at its foot
what it is: Small heaters low in the console that keep the damp out of the electronics when she lies cold.

name: Pantry unit
what it is: A low unit under the starboard side window, wholly below its sill: the cooler in its after bay, the coffee maker in a niche with a rail across it for when she rolls, and under the niche a cupboard with the mugs, the coffee, the tea and the sugar. The cupboard opens to a tap.

name: Cooler
what it is: A 45-litre refrigerator for the watch: two wire shelves, a shelf in the door. It opens to a tap.

name: Coffee maker
what it is: A filter coffee maker with a glass jug on a hot plate: a litre and a quarter, a pot for the watch. A tap on its switch starts it, and the jug fills; a tap on the jug lifts and pours it, and it empties.

name: Pantry sockets
what it is: A double 230 V socket at the back of the pantry's niche, for the coffee maker and the cooler.

name: Cable transit at the mast
what it is: Where the cables to the mast and the compass deck pass the deck, sealed gastight and watertight.

name: Cable duct on the port mullion
what it is: A covered duct down a forward mullion, from the trays over the deckhead to the console.

name: Cable duct on the starboard mullion
what it is: A covered duct down a forward mullion, from the trays over the deckhead to the console.

name: Air conditioner, room unit
what it is: The wheelhouse's cooling and dehumidifying unit, high on the aft wall over the stair.

name: Air conditioner, condensing unit
what it is: The compressor and condenser, on the compass deck above the room unit.

name: Fire hydrant, port wing
what it is: A 50 mm hydrant on the fire main, with a hose coupling and a hand valve.

name: Scupper, port wing
what it is: The wing's deck drain, led overboard.

name: Scupper, starboard wing
what it is: The wing's deck drain, led overboard.

name: Whistle valve
what it is: The valve that lets air to the whistle: opened by a solenoid from the push buttons and the fog timer, or by hand with the pull above the helm.

name: Window wash valve
what it is: A solenoid valve on the fresh-water line to the wash nozzles.

name: Window wash nozzles
what it is: A brass pipe along the windows' head outside, under the visor, with a jet over each wiper's glass.

name: Lifebuoy with light and smoke, port
what it is: A lifebuoy on a quick-release with a self-igniting light and a smoke float: thrown from the wing for a man overboard.

name: Lifebuoy with light and smoke, starboard
what it is: A lifebuoy on a quick-release with a self-igniting light and a smoke float.

name: Locker: lifejackets and pyrotechnics
what it is: Four lifejackets for the watch, twelve parachute flares and the line-throwing appliance, under the boards.

name: First-aid kit
what it is: A first-aid box under the flag locker.

name: Emergency generator set No. 1
what it is: A six-cylinder turbocharged diesel and its alternator on one skid, on six rubber mounts: 440 V, three-phase, 60 Hz, 500 kW on the owner's drawing. Its radiator stands at its forward end in a cowl, so it needs no sea water. It starts by itself when the main board is dead.

name: Starting battery bank, 24 V
what it is: Eight 12 V blocks in a steel rack, in two strings: they turn the starter, and nothing else is fed from them. The ship's transitional and radio batteries are not in this room.

name: Starting battery charger
what it is: Keeps the starting bank charged from the emergency switchboard; a voltmeter, an ammeter and a failure lamp.

name: Emergency generator control panel
what it is: Starts and stops the set, by itself or by hand; shows its voltage, frequency, load, oil pressure and temperature; the emergency stop is on its front. Fed from the starting battery.

name: Emergency switchboard, 440 V
what it is: Two sections: the generator breaker and the bus tie from the main board with their meters; and the ways to what must work when all else has stopped (steering, the emergency fire pump, emergency lighting, navigation lights, radio, alarms, the bilge pump).

name: Day tank, about 200 L
what it is: The set's own fuel, high enough to run to the engine by gravity: on a stand over a tray, with a level gauge, filled from the service tank.

name: Fuel quick-closing valve and its pull
what it is: Under the tank: shut by a wire from the red box outside the door, so that nobody goes into a fire to stop the fuel.

name: Exhaust: bellows, lagged riser, silencer
what it is: From the turbocharger through a bellows and a lagged riser up through the deckhead to a silencer on the roof.

name: Supply air duct and fire damper FD-01
what it is: Air for the engine and the room, in through a louvre on the forward wall; the damper shuts it. Its lever is worked by hand: tap it.

name: Exhaust air duct and fire damper FD-02
what it is: The room's warm air, out through a louvre on the starboard wall; the damper shuts it. Its lever is worked by hand: tap it.

name: Fuel lines
what it is: Supply from the day tank to the engine's filters and the return beside it, each tagged; the filling line from the service tank with its strainer and valve; the tank's vent, out through the wall.

name: Emergency generator room light No. 1
what it is: A fitting under the deckhead beams. Two of the four are on the emergency lighting: the one before the switchboard and the one over the way to the door.

name: Emergency generator room light No. 2
what it is: A fitting under the deckhead beams. Two of the four are on the emergency lighting: the one before the switchboard and the one over the way to the door.

name: Emergency generator room light No. 3
